description: The packages (haiccing/base-package-<name>), as the package manager writes them from this repository's modules: each a set of modules, self-contained, with what it requires. third-party is imported from the workspace's installed tree (pkgm import); the others are written from the modules (pkgm write).

third-party.description: The third-party code below mycelium, not ours: Bare's runtime and modules, the Holepunch stack, isomorphic-git, React and htm. Imported once from the development workspace (the one contact with npm), Linux x64 only, recorded in third-party.json.

mycelium.description: The repository layer: layered git repositories (mycelium-git, -layer, -repo), topics, URIs and paths; with p2p-git, git on Hyperdrive, which mycelium-git runs on.

haicc.description: HAICC: declare what a project needs, check it, make it so (haicc-reconcile), and its lifecycle (haicc-deployment). The entry package.
readme: From a folder of `haiccing` repositories side by side (clones, or plain copies), at least this one, `base-package-pkgm` and what HAICC requires (`base-package-mycelium`, `base-package-third-party`):
sh base-package-haicc/kick.sh            # step 0 (the host's prerequisites), the package manager, HAICC

Step 0 checks the host (Linux x86-64; Node.js 22 or later; git 2.25 or later; Docker Engine, rootful, native, running, and the user in the `docker` group: all needed, since nodes run in Docker containers) and fixes what is missing only with your yes (`--yes` to agree beforehand): Node.js into `~/.haicc/node` (no sudo), git and Docker Engine with `apt`. Then `haicc` is in `~/.haicc/bin`. A project (a demo) needs no kick: its `run.sh` kicks HAICC if needed.
On a machine with only `curl` and `tar` (Linux x86-64): the repositories fetched as archives and unpacked side by side, then the kick.
for r in base-package-haicc base-package-pkgm base-package-mycelium base-package-third-party; do

pkgm.description: The package manager: packages as self-contained folders, installed into the host's install folder, tested within the package. Node's built-ins only.
readme: From a folder of `haiccing` repositories side by side, this one and `base-package-haicc` (whose boot does step 0, the host's prerequisites):
sh base-package-pkgm/kick.sh   # step 0, then the package manager into ~/.haicc/packages; ~/.haicc/bin/pkgm
On a machine with only `curl` and `tar` (Linux x86-64): the repositories fetched as archives and unpacked side by side, then the kick.
for r in base-package-haicc base-package-pkgm; do

p2p.description: The p2p substrate, ours: store, discovery, connections, replication, channels, repositories on Hypercore, the name service, the node and its managers.

splectral.description: The Splectral platform: the server, its shell, the contract and model, transports, and the extensions for p2p swarms (watchers, actions, observer), scenarios, the timeline and replay; the map view (splectral/base-view-map), shared by the demos.

demo-liveness.description: Demo project: A node goes quiet. Its project (project.json), its Splectral component (splectral/base-demo-liveness), and its click and run (run.sh).

demo-other-host.description: Demo project: A node on another host. Its project (project.json), its Splectral component (splectral/base-demo-other-host), and its click and run (run.sh).
